v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (12, 12 and 13 tests). All three wrap the reply insert and the reply_count increment in DB::transaction and dispatch mail and notifications only after commit. They de-duplicate mentions case-insensitively, exclude the author with whereKeyNot, and send one private Mail::to per user plus a database notification. My probes found the same results for each: punctuation handling and '@bob's' de-duplication worked, and a forced failure in the increment rolled everything back with nothing sent. The deciding difference was the dotted-username probe. Every implementation seeds usernames with faker's userName(), and about half of those contain dots (e.g. 'john.doe'). impl-1 and impl-2 match mentions with `@(\w+)`, so those users can never be mentioned; their own factories produce data their feature can't handle. Only impl-3's regex supports dots and hyphens while trimming trailing punctuation, so it is ranked first despite weaker structure: logic in the controller, a needless empty guard, overly broad fillables and array_* functions instead of collections. impl-1 beats impl-2 on idioms and tests: Thread::addReply domain method, an author() relation, a unicode-aware /u regex, and tests for mailable rendering, the notification payload, a case-insensitive self-mention and multibyte length. Its only extra is some test noise (preventStrayRequests, forgetGuards). impl-2 is clean (an Action class plus associate), but it shares the dotted bug, lacks /u and has slightly thinner tests.
